chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Aban, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Goodness, all of it, is in the sword and beneath the shade of the sword. The people cannot be set aright except by the sword. And the swords are the keys to Paradise and the Fire.

key_terms.الجنة والنار: Paradise and the Fire — the two ultimate abodes in the afterlife
key_terms.الخير: Goodness, all that is beneficial and righteous
key_terms.السيف: The sword — symbol of jihad, military strength, and just force
key_terms.مقاليد: Keys (plural of مِقليد/مِقلاد) — means of access, instruments

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the sword in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declares that all goodness lies in the sword — in martial readiness, defense of the faith, and jihad. The sword is portrayed as the instrument by which order is established among people and the means through which one attains Paradise or avoids the Fire. This reflects the early Islamic understanding that just warfare in defense of faith and community is spiritually meritorious.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar narrated to us from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. `Imran al-Ash`ari from Muhammad b. Isma`il from `Ali b. al-Hakam from `Umar b. Aban from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
Goodness, all of it, is in the sword and beneath the shade of the sword. The people cannot be adjusted except by the sword. The swords are the keys to Paradise and the Fire.
